prerequisites: Android phone with the ScreenSync MCP app (or ADB for control tools)
steps: cd mcp-server && npm install && npm run build
npm start — the hub listens on port 3000 and prints a pairing QR + link.
Keep the hub running; the phone app and this extension both connect to it over your LAN.

envVars.SCREEN_SYNC_TOKEN: Bearer pairing token shared by app, extension and agents (default: screensync-local-dev)
envVars.SCREEN_SYNC_ADB_TARGET: Optional: pin a specific ADB device serial
envVars.SCREEN_SYNC_ADB_BIN: Optional: path to the adb binary (default: adb)

httpOnly.note: The browser extension uses this mode — no stdio needed.

httpEndpoints.purpose: SSE live stream: frame | inspection | patch | tool | agent_connect
Latest screenshot as base64 data URL
Connection state, device model, retained frames
Bug regions published by the agent
Latest git patch from the agent
status | screenshot | tap | long_press | swipe | scroll | type | key | launch

discovery.note: The phone app auto-discovers via mDNS. Browsers cannot use mDNS — the extension probes localhost and accepts manual URLs / pairing links.

troubleshooting: Hub not reachable — ensure `npm start` is running and your firewall allows port 3000 on the LAN.
401 Unauthorized — the token must match SCREEN_SYNC_TOKEN on the hub (default: screensync-local-dev).
429 Too many live connections — /api/events allows 10 concurrent clients; close another dashboard.
Extension shows offline on another machine — grant the LAN origin permission in the extension's setup step.
